header.running_head: The Advice that the Populace give to their Rulers

blocks.text:
Umar (RA) again asked him to say something, the man said, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! You start a conversation and we will talk." Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "Shame on you! Stand up. A sheep herder (like myself) can never be of any use to you?" The man stood up (and left).
When Hadhrat Umar (RA) again looked at the people, his eyes fell on a man who was also fair in complexion and thin. Hadhrat Umar (RA) motioned to him and he also came forward. When Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked him to say something, he jumped to the occasion. He praised Allaah, spoke about Allaah and then said, "You have been given charge of this Ummah, so fear Allaah with regard to the position you have been given over the Ummah and your citizens. Fear Allaah especially with regard to your personal self because you will be taken to task and questioned. You are in a position of trust and are responsible to fulfil what you have been entrusted with. You will be rewarded only according to what you do."
Hadhrat Umar (RA) then said, "Since I became the Khalifah no one besides you has ever spoken so frankly to me. Who are you?" "I am Rabee bin Ziyaad," he replied. "The brother of Muhaajir bin Ziyaad?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked. "Yes," came the reply. Hadhrat Umar (RA) then prepared some troops. He appointed the Ash'ari as commander and said to him, "Watch Rabee bin Ziyaad. If he proves true to his word, he will be of great help in your task. You may then also appoint him to a post of leadership. You should then inspect him every ten days and write to me about his conduct as a leader in so much detail that I can feel as if I had appointed him." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then added, "Rasulullaah ﷺ once advised us, 'What I fear most for you after me is the hypocrite with the tongue of a knowledgeable person.'"[^1]
The Letter that Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah (RA) and Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) Wrote to Hadhrat Umar (RA) and his Response

Hadhrat Muhammad bin Sooqa reports that he once went to Hadhrat Nu'aym bin Abu Hind who took out a paper on which the following was written:
"From Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah and Mu'aadh bin Jabal to Umar bin Khattaab.
We have observed that you are always concerned about your self reformation. You have now been given charge of this Ummah, Arabs and non-Arabs alike. You have before you people who are noble and ignoble as well as people who are enemies and those who are friends. Each of them should have their share of justice. O Umar! You should therefore watch how you deal with all of them. We caution you about a day when faces will be cast down, hearts will dry up (with fear) and all evidence will hold no weight against the evidence of the Sovereign Whose supremacy overpowers all of them. All of creation will stand before Him in
Ibn Raahway, Haarith, Musaddad and Abu Ya'la, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.7 Pg.36).
